https://telex.hu/english/2026/08/07/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar announces new measures as heatwave subsides in Hungary English Patakfalvi Dóra Andrea Horváth Kávai (translation) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Starting Friday, there is no need for voluntary cutbacks in energy consumption by companies, local governments, and the general public in Hungary any longer. The extraordinary work-from-home policy in the public sector will be lifted, decorative lighting on buildings will be turned back on, and freight trains will again be allowed to run between 5 p.m. and 10 p.m.—these were among the measures announced by Péter Magyar on Friday. According to the Hungarian Prime Minister, the Defence Task Force was able to make these decisions because, starting Saturday, the heat alert will be lowered from a level three to a level two, and the slight drop in temperature will also help reduce the strain on the country's energy grid. In addition, the Danube's catchment area has received enough rainfall to temporarily increase the river’s water level by 20–30 centimeters over the next few days, which will guarantee the safe operation of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant. Notwithstanding this, Magyar believes it is worth keeping up the attitude demonstrated in recent days, if for no other reason than because starting next week, we’ll be “counting the centimeters again” at Paks. The Prime Minister described Hungarians' recent collective effort as unprecedented, and said that initial surveys indicate that nearly every family participated in the conservation efforts. He thanked everyone who contributed in any way to resolving the crisis over the past week. https://hungarytoday.hu/right-wingers-of.text: Right-Wingers of “Our Homeland” Join Forces with the TISZA Government Against FIDESZ Dóra Dúró, MP for MHM, has explained in an interview for kontroll.hu, that their decision to join the ranks of the TISZA government is in fact in line with their electoral promise of “fighting corruption”. Her boss, Mr. Toroczkai has been a vocal critic of alleged corrupt practices under the FIDESZ government, and has a host of personal grievances against Viktor Orbán. In fact the MHM have proudly declared in a social media post from 2025 that they have voted alongside the Hungarian left in parliament 58% of the time during the last four years, and only 21% of the time alongside FIDESZ. This is very indicative of where their politics really lies, and what can one expect from them in the coming four years. Thus hopes of an informal FIDESZ-MHM alliance, or even that of a national-sovereigntist coordination against TISZA, were fundamentally put to rest with yesterday’s vote. ⚠️”Ha egy hazugságot elég sokszor ismételsz, az emberek idővel igazságnak fogják hinni.” – Pontosan ezt teszi Magyar Péter, mikor a Mi Hazánkat hazug módon szatellitpártnak nevezi, na de honnan is származik ez a kommunikációs trükk és mire megy ki a játék? 🎭Magyar Péter nincs… pic.twitter.com/zLL6pQUb6L — Mi Hazánk Mozgalom (@MiHazank) April 29, 2025 It is unlikely that Mr. Toroczkai and his MPs would soon be able to put their personal grievances against the former Orbán government to rest in view of the national interest and a shared political adversary, or indeed in view of the growing cult of personality surrounding Péter Magyar. Their greatest fear seems to be the accusation leveled against them by TISZA and other left-wing activists, namely that they are merely FIDESZ’s satellite party. In their effort to prove these critics wrong at any cost, they have managed to become mere useful pawns in the current government’s divide and rule strategy. To be fair, FIDESZ themselves have a lot to answer for this state of affairs as they made little to no effort to consolidate relations with MHM in view of the looming danger of a Brussels-sponsored proxy-government. Their inexplicable decision not to invite Mr. Toroczkai to the Tusványos Summer Camp in Romania last weekend, was just the latest insult to many previous injuries. Nevertheless, it is clear that the potentially devastating consequences of MHM casting their vote for the new Asset Recovery Office yesterday will effect the entire Hungarian national conservative sphere as a whole, including them. Those who voted for it will have to bear responsibility for the all-too-predictable overreach stemming from the unprecedented powers that this institution has been endowed with. TISZA Party MPs give themselves a round of applause after vote. Photo: MTI/Szigetváry Zsolt Fact The National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH) is intended to ensure “that the unlawful management of public assets does not go unpunished.” The goal is to identify, secure, and recover state assets that have allegedly been illegally sold under the previous government. Since the agency is to be granted hybrid powers—combining administrative, investigative, and prosecutorial (prosecutor’s office) authorities—the proposal is facing sharp criticism from multiple quarters. János Bóka, the FIDESZ parliamentary group leader, said that “If you think you can turn to another authority to challenge the arbitrariness or abuses of the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office, you are sorely mistaken. The agency can take over any proceeding at any time, and there is no legal remedy against this decision,” the politician warned. Those affected by the decisions of the new agency have neither the right to an attorney nor to general judicial protection. Legal experts and constitutional analysts also expressed concerns regarding the rule of law. The fact that the agency may, in certain cases, replace the regular public prosecutor’s office and bring charges independently undermines the principle of the separation of powers and violates the public prosecutor’s traditional monopoly on prosecution. Members of Parliament from the former governing parties, FIDESZ and KDNP (Christian Democrats), view the office as a purely politically motivated tool for political warfare. They criticize the rushed legislative process, which lacked sufficient public consultation. The planned framework conditions for the office’s leadership are adding fuel to the fire. The plan calls for extensive immunity as well as top salaries reaching millions of forints, amounting to several times the base salary of a judge. The opposition accuses the government of misusing the office for targeted political reprisals and for arbitrarily scrutinizing former government and ownership structures. Kristin Johnson O n July 25, Romuald “Rom” Lipinski celebrated his 101st birthday. Brightview Senior Living in Fair Oaks marked the milestone with a festive celebration attended by family and friends, Polish dancers, and special guests from the Embassy of the Republic of Poland in Washington, D.C. Lipinski’s extraordinary life story is one of resilience and determination, spanning multiple continents and generations. Lipinski was born in Poland in 1925. He had two older brothers, an older sister, an older step-brother and a step-sister. In September 1939, WWII broke out when Germany invaded Poland from the west. On Sept. 6, the Soviet Union invaded from the east. By early October, all of Poland was occupied. Lipinski was the only child still living at home when the NKVD, the Soviet secret police, came to deport his family. They were part of the 330,000 Polish citizens deported to parts of Siberia. Lipinski’s family began their exile in an area between Kazakhstan and Mongolia. At every location they went, his family volunteered to work. His father was a doctor, and his mother worked as a nurse and midwife. In Siberia, Lipinski carried mortar, plaster, and materials to build barracks. Lipinski sharing his life story. Kristin Johnson In June 1941, Germany invaded the Soviet Union, nullifying the two countries’ promise of non-aggression in the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. The Soviets granted the Poles they had exiled amnesty so they could create a Polish Army to fight the Germans. Lipinski’s family headed to Tashkent, Uzbekistan, where the army was to be formed. The Polish Army was not there yet, and the family was sent to Kyrgyzstan. When the Polish Army finally did form, Lipinski was too young to join. His family still traveled with the Army through Turkmenistan, and then over the Caspian Sea to Iran. Lipinski was drafted into the army in January 1943 when he was 17. He was assigned to the 12 Podolski Lancers Regiment. They were first sent to Iraq and then to Palestine. From there, they headed to Italy to join the Italian Campaign. The Battle of Monte Cassino had already been raging for over three months when his regiment arrived on April 30, 1944. When the battle ended, the Polish flag was raised over Monte Cassino. “I’ll never forget the sight as we recognized Poland, our regimental banner, on the top of Monte Cassino,” said Lipinski. “People were... crazy. Because Americans tried it, and the British tried it, New Zealanders had tried it, but we took Monte Cassino. That was a triumph.” After the war ended, Lipinski enrolled in college, first in Turin, Italy, and then in England. He struggled at first; his high school years had been chopped up by war. He studied whenever school was available to him. He is highly intelligent, but he had some catching up to do. In England, he was also learning English while he studied. Lipinski shared that he knows Polish, Russian, Italian, French, and English. In November 1951, Lipinski’s brother persuaded him to attend a dance. There he met a girl with beautiful eyes named Izabela. After that first meeting, he said that was it for him. The problem was that her family was going to the United States in the new year. They only met three times, but that was all it took for both to fall hard. According to Lipinski, Izabela was inconsolable when her family arrived in America. Eventually she came back to England, and they were married. By mid-1953, the couple arrived in the U.S. Lipinski worked and studied in the evening until he received a Master’s in Civil Engineering in 1961. They had three children and were together for 67 years before she passed away in 2019. Lipinski said that turning 101 takes a toll mentally and physically. He sleeps more, but he still enjoys playing chess and tries to keep in shape. He also enjoyed his party. There was cake and Polish delicacies for all who came to celebrate, including members of the Polish Embassy, who came for a private moment with Lipinski earlier in the day. The Wislanie Polish Folk Song and Dance Ensemble danced for about half an hour. They began with a Polonaise. Lipinski led the line of the dance as he circled the dance floor four times with a little help before sitting down to watch the rest of the festivities. https://www.politico.eu/article/ursula-v.text: BRUSSELS — Centrist parties backing European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen clashed at Thursday’s European Parliament plenary over whether to hold artificial intelligence firms accountable for harm. The EU executive had considered specific liability rules for AI in 2022, but withdrew these last year as part of the EU’s major simplification effort to make the bloc more competitive. “To withdraw the AI liability directive was a big mistake,” said Alex Agius Saliba, a Maltese vice-president of the Socialists and Democrats, part of the majority coalition. “We strongly urge the Commission to bring forward this important piece of legislation.” Advertisement Advertisement Thursday’s plenary debate, in which discussions centered on a global framework to regulate AI, showed strong tensions inside Europe between the centrist coalition backing von der Leyen. While the center-left pushed for new rules to address a series of AI-fueled hacking incidents, the center-right doubled down on simplification to ensure European companies can compete in the global AI race. Socialist and Green lawmakers called for a new AI Liability Act in a bid to hold AI companies liable for harm done by their models, as with more traditional manufacturers’ products. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman floated a similar idea for a new liability framework for companies whose models are capable of autonomous cyberattacks in the wake of this summer’s hack by autonomous OpenAI agents into another AI platform, Hugging Face. “If a phone charger explodes in your house, we never call it innovative. We call it cheap, dangerous junk, and we hold the manufacturer liable for damages,” said Dutch Green European Parliament lawmaker Kim van Sparrentak. She urged the Commission to “stop scrapping rules to please [U.S. President Donald] Trump” and come up with a “strong new liability act that covers the testing and the development of AI.” The debate quickly descended into a fierce back-and-forth between key AI-focused lawmakers from von der Leyen’s centrist coalition. Advertisement Advertisement “It feels [to] me like the Greens and the Socialists are living [on] a completely different planet than the rest of us when they are screaming for more regulation,” said Swedish center-right lawmaker Arba Kokalari, who led the work on the AI omnibus, which delayed a core section of the EU’s flagship AI law. She said the EU already had a comprehensive regulatory framework — the AI Act — of which some parts are not even into force, and said the EU should focus on avoiding falling behind in the global AI race instead. She called for “less bureaucracy, more private investments, better access to data and computing infrastructure.” Italian Social Democrat Brando Benifei, who led work on the AI Act in the previous mandate, snapped back that Europe should lead with new liability rules, “or we will need to wait for the next blogpost of a CEO to know what is happening.” German Green lawmaker Sergey Lagodinsky also fired back at Kokalari: “What planet do you live on? Not on the planet where [AI] agents break out.” International Partnerships Commissioner Jozef Síkela pointed out at the end of the debate that the rules were withdrawn because EU countries and European Parliament lawmakers couldn’t reach an agreement on them.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text: Donald Trump responded on Wednesday afternoon to a new investigation from the New York Times, which found that Mary Peltola’s Alaska Senate campaign actively recruited a man with the exact same name as Peltola’s Republican opponent in order to peel away votes. In a social media post, Trump insisted that Peltola’s actions were illegal (it’s not clear that they were) and that she should be disqualified from the race. “It has just been determined that the Democrats in Alaska illegally searched for, and recruited, a man named Dan Sullivan to run against our distinguished Republican Senator, Dan Sullivan, in order to defraud, confuse, and obfuscate the Election, thereby taking votes away from the REAL Senator, Dan Sullivan,” Trump wrote on his personal social media account.
